findings.asked: Factorise a quadratic, then solve the linked equation.
findings.wentWrong: Factorising was excellent (a few sign mix-ups). The solving part was very poor: most did not connect it with (a), and many who did wrote only the positive root.
findings.rule: Each bracket = 0 gives one solution; report both.

findings.wentWrong: Factorising was right or wrong outright. Very few used it to solve; most offered x = 5 alone, found by trial.
findings.rule: Use your factorised form - it is the method the mark scheme rewards.

findings.asked: Set up a quadratic from the information, then solve it.
findings.wentWrong: Only a handful set up the equation; many just solved the printed one, and some who factorised correctly listed only one solution.
findings.rule: Two brackets, two solutions, both on the answer line.

findings.asked: Factorise (common factor, then difference of two squares), then solve a simple quadratic.
findings.wentWrong: Taking out only 4 instead of 4a scored nothing for the first part. In the solving part weaker candidates rearranged as if the equation were linear, and some dropped the negative root.
findings.rule: A quadratic is solved by factorising or the formula, never by moving terms like a linear equation.

findings.wentWrong: About a third succeeded; many did not see the need for two brackets, signs were muddled (-12c and +27), and some wrote the brackets in x.
findings.rule: Use the letter in the question and check the signs multiply back correctly.

findings.asked: Factorise a quadratic in c, then a difference of two squares.
findings.wentWrong: Well done overall, but using x instead of c cost a mark and any wrong sign cost both.
findings.rule: Same letter as the question; signs must reproduce the middle term.

ruleToRemember: Factorise, set each bracket equal to zero, and give both solutions in the variable the question uses; part (b) almost always uses part (a).
aStarSignal: Choosing factorising over trial when a quadratic appears inside a longer problem, and stating both roots before selecting the one the context needs.
